one_liner: Fine-tune giant LLMs cheaply with LoRA/QLoRA adapters and serve thousands of them per GPU.

key_terms.definition: Family of fine-tuning methods that freeze the pretrained backbone and train a tiny fraction (often <1%) of new parameters while recovering most of full fine-tuning's quality.
PEFT method that freezes weight matrix $W_0$ and learns a low-rank update $\Delta W = \frac{\alpha}{r}BA$ added in parallel, training only the thin factors $A$ and $B$.
LoRA variant that stores the frozen base model in 4-bit NF4 precision while training a bf16 adapter on top, enabling fine-tuning of 65B-class models on a single GPU.
A 4-bit quantization data type whose 16 codebook levels sit at the quantiles of a standard normal distribution, matching the Gaussian shape of neural network weights better than uniform INT4.
QLoRA technique that quantizes the per-block fp32 absmax scaling constants themselves (to 8-bit, grouped), cutting scale-storage overhead from ~0.5 to ~0.13 bits per parameter.
QLoRA mechanism that stores optimizer state in CPU-backed unified memory, automatically evicting/reloading pages to survive transient GPU memory spikes during training instead of OOM-crashing.

LoRA refinement that decomposes each weight matrix into a magnitude vector and a direction matrix, training magnitude directly while adapting direction with a low-rank update, matching full fine-tuning more closely.
Scaling fix that replaces LoRA's $\alpha/r$ factor with $\alpha/\sqrt{r}$ so the adapter's magnitude and gradient stay stable as rank grows, letting high ranks deliver their extra capacity.
Optimizer-grouping technique that gives the $B$ matrix a learning rate $\lambda$ times larger than $A$'s (since $B$ starts at zero and must grow), improving convergence at no extra parameter cost.
Extreme PEFT variant that freezes a single shared pair of random $A,B$ matrices across all layers and trains only two small per-layer scaling vectors, shrinking adapter size 10-100x versus LoRA.
Folding a trained LoRA/DoRA update $\frac{\alpha}{r}BA$ into the frozen base weight after training, producing an ordinary linear layer with zero extra inference latency or memory.

Systems technique (S-LoRA/Punica-style) that runs one shared base-model matmul per batch and applies each request's own small adapter via a batched/segmented gather-matmul kernel, serving thousands of adapters on one GPU.

prerequisites: the Adam optimizer and its per-parameter memory cost
the transformer block (attention and MLP linear projections)
